whatItDoes: Pi Subagents adds controlled delegation, scripted multi-agent workflows, background execution, and recovery surfaces to Pi.
Each child runs under an explicit model, tool, context, and execution contract chosen by the parent workflow.

whenToReachForIt.invocation: Ask the model to use the subagent tool or invoke one of the package's operator commands.

situations.when: Independent research or review lanes can run in parallel
situations.use: Launch bounded children and aggregate their outputs.

situations.when: One parent should retain decisions while another agent implements or reviews
situations.use: Delegate the narrow role and keep final authority in the parent session.

situations.when: Long work should continue without blocking the interactive session
situations.use: Run the child in the background and recover through persisted status.

whatItAdds: One model-invoked delegation tool with sequential and parallel workflow controls.
Background lifecycle, wait, recovery, and operator-facing command surfaces.

howItFits.relationship: Subagents divide work inside an orchestration; handoff moves selected context to a fresh top-level session.
Visual Explainer can recommend a subagent context-gathering pass before rendering.
Ralph governs durable task iterations; subagents provide bounded execution and review lanes within them.

questions.question: What are the operating costs?
answer: Each child consumes model time and may receive narrower context or tools; this setup reviews the installed revision, not current upstream main.

workingIf: The parent receives a completed child result or a recoverable background status.
Child tools and context match the contract supplied at launch.
setupNotes: Created and maintained by Nico Bailon; installed directly from the original MIT-licensed project.
The package is installed from its Git repository and depends on Pi package APIs plus child model and tool configuration.
Behavior claims were reviewed against the installed revision rather than a moving branch.
